explainer.summary: WETH9 is a simple ERC20 wrapper for ETH with no owner or admin. Users send ETH via deposit() or fallback to mint WETH and call withdraw() to redeem ETH 1:1. All state is in public balanceOf/allowance mappings; totalSupply equals contract ETH balance.

key_functions.name: deposit
key_functions.what: payable; increases msg.sender balanceOf by msg.value and emits Deposit

key_functions.name: withdraw
key_functions.what: requires sufficient balanceOf, subtracts wad, sends ETH via transfer, emits Withdrawal

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: sets allowance[msg.sender][guy] = wad and emits Approval

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: calls transferFrom(msg.sender, dst, wad)

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: checks src balance, deducts allowance unless infinite, moves tokens, emits Transfer

key_functions.name: totalSupply
key_functions.what: returns this.balance (contract ETH holdings)

key_functions.name: fallback
key_functions.what: calls deposit()

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; immutable contract with no proxy or owner logic.
user_risks: Classic unlimited allowance pattern (uint(-1)) used in transferFrom
withdraw relies on .transfer which may fail on receivers with high gas use
No reentrancy guard; external call in withdraw after state update
integration_tips: Send ETH to contract address or call deposit() to obtain WETH
Use approve + transferFrom for spending; check for infinite allowance
Call withdraw to unwrap; ensure sufficient gas for receiver

explainer.summary: TetherToken implements an ERC20 token with owner-controlled pausing, blacklisting, fee-on-transfer, minting/redeeming, and a deprecation flag that forwards calls to an UpgradedStandardToken at upgradedAddress. All state-changing ERC20 operations (transfer, transferFrom, approve) first check !paused and !isBlackListed before applying optional fees or delegating. Ownership, blacklist, pause, issue/redeem, and parameter changes are restricted to the single owner address set at construction.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Moves tokens after checking not paused and not blacklisted; applies basisPointsRate/maximumFee if set, sending fee to owner; delegates to upgradedAddress.transferByLegacy when deprecated.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens using allowance after the same pause/blacklist checks; applies fee logic and reduces allowance unless MAX_UINT; delegates when deprecated.

key_functions.name: issue
key_functions.what: Only owner: increases _totalSupply and owner balance after overflow checks.

key_functions.name: redeem
key_functions.what: Only owner: decreases _totalSupply and owner balance after sufficient-balance checks.

key_functions.name: addBlackList
key_functions.what: Only owner: sets isBlackListed[_evilUser] = true.

key_functions.name: destroyBlackFunds
key_functions.what: Only owner: requires blacklisted, zeros balance and subtracts from _totalSupply.

key_functions.name: deprecate
key_functions.what: Only owner: sets deprecated=true and upgradedAddress.

key_functions.name: setParams
key_functions.what: Only owner: sets basisPointsRate (<20) and maximumFee (<50*10^decimals).

admin_powers: pause / unpause the contract
add/remove addresses from blacklist
destroy all funds of a blacklisted address
issue or redeem tokens to/from owner
set transfer fee parameters
transfer ownership
deprecate contract and point to upgradedAddress
explainer.upgradeability: When deprecated is true, transfer/transferFrom/approve/balanceOf/allowance/totalSupply forward to the corresponding ByLegacy or direct methods on the UpgradedStandardToken at upgradedAddress; otherwise execute locally.
user_risks: contract can be paused by owner, blocking transfers
owner can blacklist any address and permanently destroy its tokens
transfer fees (up to 20 bp, capped) are sent to owner
owner can mint or burn arbitrary amounts via issue/redeem
owner can replace the entire implementation via deprecate
integration_tips: always read totalSupply/balanceOf through the current contract; they may delegate when deprecated
check !isBlackListed[msg.sender] and !paused before assuming transfers will succeed
approve must be called with value 0 first if changing a non-zero allowance
monitor Deprecate, Issue, Redeem, Params, AddedBlackList events for state changes

explainer.summary: FiatTokenV2_2 extends FiatTokenV2_1 to introduce a packed balanceAndBlacklistStates storage layout, an initializeV2_2 migration that updates the token symbol and moves accounts from _deprecatedBlacklisted, and an EIP712 domain separator using version "2" plus chainid(). It overrides approve, permit (both v/r/s and signature bytes forms), increase/decreaseAllowance, and the four authorization functions while adding whenNotPaused and notBlacklisted guards.

key_functions.name: initializeV2_2
key_functions.what: Requires _initializedVersion==2, sets symbol=newSymbol, migrates listed accounts from _deprecatedBlacklisted into _blacklist, blacklists the contract itself, then sets _initializedVersion=3.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Two overloads (bytes signature and v/r/s) that call _permit after whenNotPaused check.

key_functions.name: transferWithAuthorization
key_functions.what: Calls _transferWithAuthorization after whenNotPaused and notBlacklisted checks on from/to.

key_functions.name: receiveWithAuthorization
key_functions.what: Calls _receiveWithAuthorization after whenNotPaused and notBlacklisted checks on from/to.

key_functions.name: cancelAuthorization
key_functions.what: Calls _cancelAuthorization after whenNotPaused check.

key_functions.name: _setBlacklistState
key_functions.what: Sets high bit of balanceAndBlacklistStates via OR or resets to _balanceOf depending on _shouldBlacklist.

key_functions.name: _setBalance
key_functions.what: Rejects balances > (2^255-1) or blacklisted accounts, then stores value in lower 255 bits.

key_functions.name: _isBlacklisted
key_functions.what: Returns true if high bit of balanceAndBlacklistStates is set.

key_functions.name: _balanceOf
key_functions.what: Returns lower 255 bits of balanceAndBlacklistStates masked by ((1<<255)-1).

key_functions.name: _chainId
key_functions.what: Returns current chainid via inline assembly.

admin_powers: initializeV2_2 may be called once (when _initializedVersion==2) to change symbol and migrate the blacklist
explainer.upgradeability: Initialization-based upgrade via initializeV2_2 that checks _initializedVersion and writes _initializedVersion=3; domain separator and blacklist logic are overridden for the new storage layout.
user_risks: Blacklisted accounts cannot transfer or have balances updated
Balances cannot exceed (2^255-1)
Signed permits and authorizations are subject to deadline/validBefore and nonce checks
integration_tips: Call initializeV2_2 with the full list of accountsToBlacklist and desired newSymbol during the upgrade step
Use the bytes-signature permit/authorization overloads for EOA wallets (r,s,v packing order)
Query _balanceOf and _isBlacklisted rather than direct storage reads because of the packed layout

explainer.summary: The Dai contract is an ERC20 token implementing the DAI stablecoin with authorization via wards, mint/burn controlled by auth, and EIP-712 permit support. It inherits LibNote for logging and uses DOMAIN_SEPARATOR for permit signatures. No proxy or delegatecall patterns are present in the source.

key_functions.name: rely
key_functions.what: Grants ward status to an address via auth modifier and note event.

key_functions.name: deny
key_functions.what: Revokes ward status from an address via auth modifier and note event.

key_functions.name: mint
key_functions.what: Increases balance and totalSupply for usr, callable only by wards.

key_functions.name: burn
key_functions.what: Decreases balance and totalSupply for usr after allowance check.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens with allowance deduction unless infinite allowance.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowance and emits Approval event.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Sets allowance via EIP-712 signature after nonce, expiry and ecrecover checks.

key_functions.name: push
key_functions.what: Alias calling transferFrom from msg.sender.

key_functions.name: pull
key_functions.what: Alias calling transferFrom to msg.sender.

key_functions.name: move
key_functions.what: Alias calling transferFrom between src and dst.

admin_powers: rely(address)
deny(address)
mint(address,uint256)
explainer.upgradeability: No upgradeability; contract has no proxy, delegatecall or storage gap patterns.
user_risks: Wards can mint arbitrary supply
Single point of authorization failure if wards compromised
Permit requires correct nonce and expiry or reverts
integration_tips: Check allowance != uint(-1) before assuming deduction in transferFrom
Use DOMAIN_SEPARATOR and PERMIT_TYPEHASH for off-chain signatures
Call rely/deny only from initial ward set in constructor

explainer.summary: UniswapV2Factory (constructor takes _feeToSetter) deploys UniswapV2Pair instances via create2 in createPair and maintains getPair and allPairs mappings/arrays; it exposes feeTo and feeToSetter state that control protocol fee collection inside pair _mintFee. All pair creation and admin setters are permissioned only to the initial feeToSetter. The contract contains no selfdestruct, delegatecall, or proxy logic.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Sets feeToSetter to the provided address; feeTo remains address(0).

key_functions.name: createPair
key_functions.what: Validates distinct non-zero tokens, deploys a UniswapV2Pair with create2 using salt from token0/token1, calls initialize, records the pair, and emits PairCreated.

key_functions.name: setFeeTo
key_functions.what: Allows feeToSetter to update the feeTo address used by pairs for protocol fee minting.

key_functions.name: setFeeToSetter
key_functions.what: Allows current feeToSetter to transfer the setter role to a new address.

key_functions.name: getPair
key_functions.what: Returns the pair address for any token0/token1 combination (populated bidirectionally).

key_functions.name: allPairs
key_functions.what: Returns the pair address at a given index in the allPairs array.

key_functions.name: allPairsLength
key_functions.what: Returns the length of the allPairs array.

admin_powers: feeToSetter can call setFeeTo to designate the recipient of protocol fees minted in pairs.
feeToSetter can call setFeeToSetter to transfer administrative control to any address.
explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable: no proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade mechanism exists in UniswapV2Factory or its libraries.
user_risks: feeToSetter is a single trusted address that can redirect all future protocol fees.
createPair will revert if a pair already exists or if tokens are identical or zero-address.
Pairs rely on the factory address stored at deployment; any factory replacement would require separate migration.
integration_tips: Call createPair only from contracts that have already verified tokenA != tokenB and allowance/balance checks.
Use getPair[token0][token1] (with canonical ordering) to obtain the deterministic pair address without deployment.
Monitor PairCreated events to index all pairs; allPairsLength provides the current count for enumeration.

explainer.summary: UniswapV2Router02 is a non-upgradeable contract (constructor sets immutable factory and WETH) that routes liquidity and swap operations to Uniswap V2 pairs via the factory. It implements IUniswapV2Router02, enforces deadlines with the ensure modifier, and delegates core math to UniswapV2Library and SafeMath. All external calls require explicit path, amount, and deadline parameters; no owner or admin state exists.

key_functions.name: addLiquidity
key_functions.what: Adds liquidity to a token pair after optionally creating the pair and computing optimal amounts.

key_functions.name: addLiquidityETH
key_functions.what: Adds liquidity using ETH, wrapping via WETH and refunding excess ETH.

key_functions.name: removeLiquidity
key_functions.what: Burns LP tokens and returns underlying tokens after minimum-amount checks.

key_functions.name: removeLiquidityETH
key_functions.what: Removes liquidity and unwraps WETH to ETH for the caller.

key_functions.name: swapExactTokensForTokens
key_functions.what: Swaps an exact input amount along a path, enforcing amountOutMin and deadline.

key_functions.name: swapExactETHForTokens
key_functions.what: Swaps ETH for tokens via WETH deposit and _swap, enforcing amountOutMin.

key_functions.name: swapExactTokensForETH
key_functions.what: Swaps tokens for ETH via WETH withdrawal after _swap.

key_functions.name: _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens
key_functions.what: Internal swap loop that reads post-transfer balances to handle fee-on-transfer tokens.

key_functions.name: getAmountsOut
key_functions.what: View wrapper returning cumulative output amounts for a given path via UniswapV2Library.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; immutable factory and WETH set once in constructor with no proxy or owner logic.
user_risks: Deadline must be >= block.timestamp or transaction reverts with EXPIRED.
All swaps and liquidity ops require amountMin checks; insufficient output reverts.
Fee-on-transfer tokens use separate supporting functions; standard swap functions may under-deliver.
ETH refunds occur only for excess in addLiquidityETH and swapETHForExactTokens.
integration_tips: Always pass a future deadline and set slippage tolerances via amountMin parameters.
Use the SupportingFeeOnTransferTokens variants when the path may contain fee tokens.
Verify path[0] == WETH for ETH swaps and path[last] == WETH for ETH outputs.
Call getAmountsOut or getAmountsIn first to compute expected values before sending transactions.

explainer.summary: SwapRouter is a stateless contract for executing exact-input and exact-output swaps (single-hop or multi-hop) against Uniswap V3 pools via the uniswapV3SwapCallback mechanism. It inherits PeripheryImmutableState (factory + WETH9 set at construction), PeripheryValidation (deadline checks), PeripheryPaymentsWithFee, Multicall, and SelfPermit; all swap logic lives in exactInputInternal/exactOutputInternal and the four public entrypoints. No mutable admin state or upgrade logic exists in the provided source.

key_functions.name: exactInputSingle
key_functions.what: Performs a single-pool exact-input swap with amountOutMinimum and sqrtPriceLimitX96 checks.

key_functions.name: exactInput
key_functions.what: Walks a multi-pool path performing chained exact-input swaps, updating payer to address(this) after the first hop.

key_functions.name: exactOutputSingle
key_functions.what: Performs a single-pool exact-output swap, resetting amountInCached afterward.

key_functions.name: exactOutput
key_functions.what: Initiates an exact-output swap (possibly multi-hop) and reads the final amountIn from the transient amountInCached variable.

key_functions.name: uniswapV3SwapCallback
key_functions.what: Validates the pool callback, decodes SwapCallbackData, pays the required tokenIn (or continues the next hop for exact-output).

key_functions.name: multicall
key_functions.what: Executes an array of delegatecalls to this contract and returns the results or reverts with the inner revert string.

key_functions.name: selfPermit
key_functions.what: Calls permit on an ERC20Permit token to approve the router without a separate transaction.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; constructor sets immutable factory and WETH9, no proxy or owner-controlled logic present.
user_risks: Deadline must be respected or the call reverts with 'Transaction too old'.
amountOutMinimum / amountInMaximum must be set correctly to protect against slippage.
sqrtPriceLimitX96 can be used to restrict price impact but is optional.
integration_tips: Batch approvals and swaps in a single multicall using selfPermit* functions.
For multi-hop exactInput, the path bytes must be correctly encoded with token-fee-token segments.
Recipient can be address(0) to custody intermediate tokens at the router.

explainer.summary: Permit2 inherits from SignatureTransfer and AllowanceTransfer (both inheriting EIP712) to unify signature-based and allowance-based ERC20 transfers under a single contract with EIP-712 domain separation and cross-chain replay protection via cached chainid. All transfer paths require prior token approvals to Permit2 and enforce deadlines, nonces, and amount checks before calling safeTransferFrom. The contract contains no owner, proxy, or upgrade logic.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Updates amount and expiration in the allowance mapping for a token-spender pair.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Verifies a PermitSingle or PermitBatch signature, then calls _updateApproval to set allowance details.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens using stored PackedAllowance, checking expiration and decrementing amount if not max.

key_functions.name: lockdown
key_functions.what: Zeros the amount for each TokenSpenderPair supplied by the caller.

key_functions.name: invalidateNonces
key_functions.what: Advances the nonce in a PackedAllowance, subject to delta <= type(uint16).max.

key_functions.name: permitTransferFrom
key_functions.what: Consumes an unordered nonce, verifies signature, and executes safeTransferFrom for single or batch permits.

key_functions.name: permitWitnessTransferFrom
key_functions.what: Same as permitTransferFrom but includes an additional witness hash in the typed data.

key_functions.name: invalidateUnorderedNonces
key_functions.what: Sets bits in nonceBitmap[msg.sender][wordPos] to mark nonces as used.

explainer.upgradeability: No upgradeability; EIP712 stores immutable _CACHED_DOMAIN_SEPARATOR and _CACHED_CHAIN_ID with no proxy or delegatecall patterns present.
user_risks: Signatures become invalid after sigDeadline or permit.deadline, reverting with SignatureExpired.
Nonces must match exactly or _useUnorderedNonce / _updateApproval will revert with InvalidNonce.
Allowances expire based on block.timestamp and can be reduced by concurrent transfers.
Batch operations require exact length match between permitted and transferDetails arrays.
integration_tips: Call DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() to obtain the current EIP-712 domain for off-chain signing.
Approve Permit2 on each token before using any transfer or permit function.
Use invalidateUnorderedNonces or invalidateNonces to prevent replay after a permit is consumed.
For contract wallets, implement IERC1271.isValidSignature as required by SignatureVerification.

explainer.summary: The Uni contract implements the UNI governance token as an EIP-20 with 1e9 initial supply, 18 decimals, and built-in vote delegation via checkpoints. Minting is restricted to a single minter address that can only act after a timestamp and is limited to 2% of supply once per year. It also provides EIP-2612 permit and EIP-712 delegation-by-signature.

key_functions.name: mint
key_functions.what: Allows the current minter to create new tokens up to the mintCap after mintingAllowedAfter, updating totalSupply and delegating votes.

key_functions.name: setMinter
key_functions.what: Transfers the minter role to a new address; callable only by the existing minter.

key_functions.name: delegate
key_functions.what: Delegates the caller's voting power to another address and records the change via checkpoints.

key_functions.name: delegateBySig
key_functions.what: Delegates votes using an EIP-712 signature, validating nonce, expiry and chainId.

key_functions.name: getPriorVotes
key_functions.what: Returns the vote balance of an account at a specific past block number using binary search over checkpoints.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Sets allowance via EIP-712 signature, supporting infinite approval and deadline checks.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens while decreasing the spender's allowance unless it is the maximum value.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets the allowance for a spender, with special handling for uint(-1) as infinite.

admin_powers: The minter can call mint subject to time and cap limits
The minter can call setMinter to transfer the role
explainer.upgradeability: None; the contract has no proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade mechanism.
user_risks: A single minter address can mint up to 2% of supply annually after the initial delay
Approvals are subject to the known ERC-20 race condition described in the approve comment
Vote checkpoints are written only on transfer or delegation; balances alone do not update votes
integration_tips: Use getPriorVotes for governance snapshots rather than balanceOf at the current block
Call delegate or delegateBySig immediately after receiving tokens to activate voting power
Check allowances[src][spender] == uint96(-1) to detect infinite approvals before transferFrom

explainer.summary: LinkToken is a fixed-supply ERC20 token (totalSupply=10**27) that also implements ERC677 via ERC677Token for transferAndCall. All tokens are assigned to the deployer in the constructor; transfers, approvals and transferFrom are guarded by the validRecipient modifier that blocks address(0) and the token itself. The contract contains no owner, mint, burn or pause logic.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Moves tokens from msg.sender to _to after validRecipient check, using SafeMath.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens from _from to _to using allowance, after validRecipient check.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowance for _spender after validRecipient check.

key_functions.name: increaseApproval
key_functions.what: Adds to the current allowance for _spender.

key_functions.name: decreaseApproval
key_functions.what: Subtracts from the current allowance, flooring at zero.

key_functions.name: transferAndCall
key_functions.what: Calls super.transfer then Transfer event with data and onTokenTransfer if _to is a contract, after validRecipient check.

key_functions.name: balanceOf
key_functions.what: Returns the stored balance for an address.

key_functions.name: allowance
key_functions.what: Returns the remaining allowance from owner to spender.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; the contract has no proxy, owner or delegatecall mechanisms.
user_risks: Classic ERC20 approve race condition remains possible despite increase/decreaseApproval helpers.
transferAndCall will silently succeed if the recipient contract's onTokenTransfer reverts are not handled by the caller.
integration_tips: Use transferAndCall when sending to a contract that implements ERC677Receiver to receive the data callback.
Call increaseApproval/decreaseApproval instead of approve when the current allowance is non-zero.
All transfers reject the zero address and the token contract itself via validRecipient.

explainer.summary: GnosisSafe v1.3.0 is the singleton master copy for a multisig wallet supporting EIP-712 SafeTx hashes, multiple signature types (ECDSA, contract, approvedHash, eth_sign) and optional Guard/Fallback handlers. The constructor sets threshold=1 to prevent direct use; setup (callable only once) configures owners/threshold/modules/fallbackHandler via setupOwners/setupModules/internalSetFallbackHandler while execTransaction increments nonce, checks signatures via checkNSignatures and optionally runs Guard checks before/after execute. All state-changing admin actions after setup must occur through execTransaction because of the SelfAuthorized modifier.

key_functions.name: setup
key_functions.what: Initializes owners, threshold, fallbackHandler, modules and optional payment; emits SafeSetup.

key_functions.name: execTransaction
key_functions.what: Encodes tx data, increments nonce, verifies signatures with checkSignatures, runs guard checks, executes via Executor.execute and handles payment.

key_functions.name: checkSignatures
key_functions.what: Loads threshold and calls checkNSignatures to require _threshold valid signatures.

key_functions.name: checkNSignatures
key_functions.what: Iterates signatures, handles v=0 (contract), v=1 (approvedHash), v>30 (eth_sign) and default ecrecover, enforcing owner ordering and SENTINEL_OWNERS rules.

key_functions.name: approveHash
key_functions.what: Marks a hash as approved by msg.sender owner; emits ApproveHash.

key_functions.name: encodeTransactionData
key_functions.what: Builds EIP-712 encoded bytes using SAFE_TX_TYPEHASH, domainSeparator and all tx/payment/nonce fields.

key_functions.name: getTransactionHash
key_functions.what: Returns keccak256 of encodeTransactionData result.

key_functions.name: handlePayment
key_functions.what: Calculates gasUsed+baseGas payment in ETH or ERC20 and transfers to receiver (tx.origin if unset).

key_functions.name: setGuard
key_functions.what: Authorized function storing guard address in GUARD_STORAGE_SLOT.

key_functions.name: setFallbackHandler
key_functions.what: Authorized function storing handler in FALLBACK_HANDLER_STORAGE_SLOT.

admin_powers: setGuard (via authorized exec)
setFallbackHandler (via authorized exec)
setupOwners and setupModules (only inside initial setup)
addOwnerWithThreshold/removeOwner/swapOwner/changeThreshold (via OwnerManager after setup)
explainer.upgradeability: No upgrade logic present; contract is the immutable singleton master copy referenced by GnosisSafeProxy instances via the first storage slot.
user_risks: Incorrect gas parameters (safeTxGas, baseGas, gasPrice) can cause GS010/GS013 reverts or loss of refund
Signature ordering and owner checks in checkNSignatures can reject otherwise valid multisig sets
Guard can block or revert any transaction
Fallback handler receives arbitrary calldata and must be trusted
integration_tips: Always obtain the tx hash via getTransactionHash before collecting signatures
When using gas refunds set gasPrice>0 and refundReceiver appropriately
Use StorageAccessible methods instead of the deprecated requiredTxGas
Deploy via official proxy factory so the singleton remains untouched

explainer.summary: Multicall3 aggregates results from multiple function calls into one transaction and is backwards-compatible with Multicall and Multicall2. It defines Call, Call3, Call3Value, and Result structs and implements aggregate, tryAggregate, aggregate3, aggregate3Value plus block and chain query helpers, all using low-level .call. The contract contains no owner, admin, or upgrade logic.

key_functions.name: aggregate
key_functions.what: Executes Call[] requiring every call to succeed, returns blockNumber and returnData array.

key_functions.name: tryAggregate
key_functions.what: Executes Call[] with optional requireSuccess flag, returns Result[] containing success and returnData for each.

key_functions.name: tryBlockAndAggregate
key_functions.what: Calls tryAggregate and also returns current blockNumber and blockHash.

key_functions.name: blockAndAggregate
key_functions.what: Wrapper that calls tryBlockAndAggregate with requireSuccess=true.

key_functions.name: aggregate3
key_functions.what: Executes Call3[] allowing per-call allowFailure, reverts on failure when not allowed using inline assembly.

key_functions.name: aggregate3Value
key_functions.what: Executes Call3Value[] forwarding per-call value, enforces msg.value equals sum of values, reverts on mismatch or disallowed failure.

key_functions.name: getBlockNumber
key_functions.what: Returns block.number.

key_functions.name: getEthBalance
key_functions.what: Returns address balance via addr.balance.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; the contract contains no proxy, owner, or upgrade logic.
user_risks: Low-level .call is used; target contracts may perform arbitrary state changes or reentrancy.
aggregate3Value reverts if msg.value does not exactly equal the sum of call values.
When allowFailure is false, any failing subcall causes the entire multicall to revert.
integration_tips: Prefer aggregate3 or aggregate3Value when partial failures are acceptable.
When using aggregate3Value, compute and send the exact total value required by the Call3Value array.
Always inspect the success field of each Result when allowFailure is true.

explainer.summary: ENSRegistryWithFallback extends ENSRegistry and adds a fallback to a prior ENS instance stored in the immutable 'old' field set at construction. View functions (owner, resolver, ttl) check recordExists on the current mapping and delegate to old.* if absent; writes use the inherited authorised modifier and _setOwner logic. The root node (0x0) owner is set to the deployer in ENSRegistry.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Calls ENSRegistry() then stores the provided ENS _old into the public old field.

key_functions.name: resolver
key_functions.what: Returns super.resolver(node) if recordExists(node) else old.resolver(node).

key_functions.name: owner
key_functions.what: Returns super.owner(node) if recordExists(node) else old.owner(node); super.owner maps address(this) to 0x0.

key_functions.name: ttl
key_functions.what: Returns super.ttl(node) if recordExists(node) else old.ttl(node).

key_functions.name: setOwner
key_functions.what: Authorised modifier check then _setOwner and Transfer event.

key_functions.name: setSubnodeOwner
key_functions.what: Authorised check, computes keccak256(node,label), calls _setOwner, emits NewOwner.

key_functions.name: setApprovalForAll
key_functions.what: Sets operators[msg.sender][operator] and emits ApprovalForAll.

key_functions.name: _setOwner
key_functions.what: Internal: if owner==0x0 stores address(this) instead, then records[node].owner=addr.

admin_powers: Initial owner of node 0x0 (set in ENSRegistry constructor)
Any address that passes the authorised modifier (owner or approved operator)
explainer.upgradeability: No proxy; migration is achieved by the fallback reads to the immutable 'old' ENS instance for nodes not yet present in the new registry.
user_risks: Setting owner to address(0) stores address(this) instead, making the contract the owner.
Operators stored in the operators mapping can call any authorised function on the owner's behalf.
integration_tips: Call owner/resolver/ttl to obtain values transparently from either registry.
Use recordExists to determine whether a node has been written to the new registry.
setRecord and setSubnodeRecord combine owner+resolver+ttl updates in one call.

explainer.summary: Seaport 1.5 is a thin contract inheriting from Consideration that accepts a conduitController address in its constructor and overrides _name/_nameString to return "Seaport". All transfer logic, including native/ERC20/ERC721/ERC1155 handling via direct calls or conduits, is implemented in the inherited Executor contract using accumulator-based batching.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Accepts conduitController address and passes it to Consideration base constructor.

key_functions.name: _name
key_functions.what: Internal pure function returning contract name via assembly as "Seaport".

key_functions.name: _nameString
key_functions.what: Internal pure function returning the string "Seaport" for name hash derivation.

key_functions.name: _transfer
